front: Parts of the hen's oviduct in order
back: Infundibulum (fertilisation), magnum (albumen), isthmus (shell membranes), uterus/shell gland (shell), vagina (cuticle; laying).
Two testes inside the body near the kidneys; two sperm ducts open into the cloaca; mating by cloacal contact; no scrotum.

front: Which ovary works in a hen?
back: Only the left ovary and left oviduct develop.

front: How long does an egg take to form?
back: About a day (roughly 24-26 hours), most of it in the shell gland.
Thin coat sealing the shell pores against bacteria and water loss; washing removes it.
Chalazae: cords holding the yolk central. Air cell: space at the broad end; air for the chick; grows as the egg ages.
Fertility = fertile ÷ set × 100. Hatchability = hatched ÷ fertile × 100 (or ÷ set).

front: Do hens need a cock to lay?
back: No. A cock is needed only for fertile eggs; incubation of fertile eggs takes 21 days.
